entries.section: (1) Opening greeting

paragraphs.text: Bishops: in Greek the word means overseers of the churches. It refers to the bishops and the priests, their assistants, who are responsible for the care of the people.

Deacons: in Syriac, servants. They are the helpers in the care of the people together with the bishops and the priests. St. Paul joins the name of his disciple Timothy to his own without distinction or discrimination, making his disciple equal to himself, which shows his humility. Paul feels that he belongs to God, for He bought him with His precious blood, so that he became His servant, and the servant has only to obey his master. He refrained from going to places where he wished to go, and went in obedience to God's command in the vision in which the man of Macedonia appeared to him saying, "Come over to us and help us" (Acts 16:9). He sends his greeting to the saints in Christ Jesus who are believers, and singles out the shepherds because they represent all the people whom they shepherd.

entries.section: (1) Opening greeting

paragraphs.text: Grace was the greeting with which the Greeks began their letters, and peace is the Hebrew greeting with which the Jews greeted one another. Therefore St. Paul was accustomed always to join these two greetings in his letters, to show that Christ is for everyone.

Submission to the will of God gives a person rest. So accept His will in your life in the difficult matters that come upon you, or those that run contrary to your plans, confident that it is better than what you would have arranged, and Christ will bear the responsibility for you and give you peace.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul thanks God whenever he remembers the people of Philippi, because of their faith and their love.

May we thank God for the many blessings with which He has favored us. This is what the Church teaches us, for she begins her prayers on all occasions with the prayer of thanksgiving, because thanksgiving makes you aware of the grace of God that is with you. So be confident in yourself, upheld by God, and rejoice in His work in you.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul remembers them always whenever he prays, mingling thanksgiving with supplication.

He prays with joy despite the harassment of those who oppose him and the hardship of prison and chains, because he feels the presence of Christ with him and rejoices in the growth of the ministry although he is bound in prison.
May we not stand before God every time only to ask and ask and forget to thank Him, and when we ask, may we not forget to ask on behalf of others.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul prays and thanks God for the love of the people of Philippi, who contributed to the needs of the preaching of the Gospel from the first day on which they were brought to faith until this time in which he writes his letter as a prisoner, a period of nearly ten years.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: Paul is confident that God, who gave them the grace of giving, is able to establish them in this virtue until His Second Coming, that they may rejoice with Him in heaven.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul shows his fatherhood not only in praying for the people of Philippi, but in his love and his constant feeling for them, even in the midst of tribulations, while in the chains of prison and while preaching and defending the Gospel. He praises them as his partners in the grace of preaching, because they helped him in his material needs, so that they have the reward of preaching just as he does.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul calls God to witness to the truth of his words concerning the tender feelings and affections he bears for them all. These are not feelings of human love but spiritual love, which he received from Christ, who loved them with a deep love (bowels), so that He gave Himself for them.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: The Apostle prays always for them that their love for God and for people may grow more and more, a love founded on knowledge and spiritual understanding.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: True love for God grants a person an enlightened mind and the virtue of discerning between conflicting matters, so that he chooses what is good among them and leaves what is not good. Thus we do not halt between two sides, nor do we sow any confusion of thought in the holy Church, and we continue in our faithfulness to the Gospel and avoid stumbling until the day of Christ's Second Coming.

entries.section: (2) Paul's love and his prayers for them

paragraphs.text: The righteous Christian must bear fruit, and the fruit of righteousness is good works. But let us know that this fruit is not from ourselves but is from God and to the glory of God.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: The Apostle reassures the people of Philippi that his imprisonment did not hinder the preaching of the Gospel, but on the contrary was a cause of the advance of preaching in Rome.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: It has now become known to everyone that his chains are not because of any offense he committed, but because of his faith in Christ. The preaching has spread, not only in the governor's palace through each soldier of the imperial guard whose hand was bound to the hand of St. Paul during his watch, but in all other places as well.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: When the brethren saw Paul's preaching while a prisoner and saw his joy in the midst of sufferings, they were filled with zeal and fervor, and preached the name of Christ without fear.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: There were some who preached Christ to the people while their hearts overflowed with envy of Paul and jealousy toward him, hoping to gain a better renown and reputation than his. But there are others who are sincere in their preaching, who do it out of love and a genuine desire for the salvation of souls.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: There are those who preach for personal gain and selfish ambition, and this is the correct translation of the original Greek word rendered in Arabic "contention." They aim to obtain people's esteem and the glorifying of themselves. These are insincere in their preaching and their proclaiming of Christ, and their aim is to trouble St. Paul and fight him, and they wish to torment him with a mental torment more severe than the torment of the iron chains with which he is bound in his prison.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: But the others teach with the mind of Christ, and they are impelled to preach by love for God and for people, knowing that St. Paul is appointed by divine providence to spread the Gospel.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul shows his attitude toward all of these, and asks, saying: What then ... Then he answers that whether the preaching is out of self-glorification or out of pure love for God, he rejoices in every case in the spread of the joyful message and the spread of the name of Christ, and he rejoices also because God will turn evil into good.

Accept other opinions that oppose yours if they are useful and constructive. The difference of opinions should not disturb you; rather encourage it, since it means that others are concerned about the matter, and this is not against your dignity. And if you are disturbed, know that there is pride within you and that you need repentance.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: The Apostle knows with certainty that every persecution turns into a credit that secures for him the salvation to which he looks forward upon entering eternity, through their prayers and the support of the Holy Spirit, that is, the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

entries.section: (3) The spread of the Gospel

paragraphs.text: All that he awaits and hopes for is that he not fail in his preaching but boldly proclaim his witness to Christ at all times, so that the name of Christ may be glorified through his bodily sufferings and his chains, and even his death and martyrdom will proclaim the life of Christ in him.

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: For me to live is Christ: this phrase shows us the Apostle's mind, for he sees his life hidden in Christ, that is, Christ for him is the center of life and the center of thought and is everything. To die is gain: the Apostle looks at death as a means of departing from the world to blessed eternity, and a departure from the prison of the body to the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: The work of preaching and the abundant fruit that the Apostle gathers into the fold of Christ leave him in perplexity as to which to choose: life, where he serves his brethren, or death, where he will be with Christ?

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: These two desires dominate him: the desire to depart from the captivity of the body to the Kingdom of Heaven, where he will be with Christ all the time, enjoying life with Him, a spiritual enjoyment that no other enjoyment equals.

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: But for their good and their spiritual benefit and their progress in the spiritual life, it is more necessary that he remain in the flesh with them.

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: He is confident that his remaining in the flesh fulfills the divine will, because it is necessary for their progress and their joy in the faith in Christ.

entries.section: (4) Life and death

paragraphs.text: Your rejoicing in Christ Jesus: your glorifying of God.

His remaining in the flesh increases their glorifying of the Lord. They will also rejoice at his return to them and his presence in their midst in fullness of blessing and grace after his release from prison.

How beautiful it is that you make heaven your only goal, and if you look to the earth you seek your salvation and the salvation of those around you, preparing for the Kingdom every day. Then you will experience the presence of God with you and receive the earnest of the Kingdom, which increases your longing for it until you depart toward it. And if you are occupied with the goals of the world, such as money, position, relationships and various lusts, may you repent and return quickly to your goal.

entries.section: (5) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Only: here it means that what he will now say to them as a commandment is the conclusion of the whole matter.

Paul asks them to live in a manner worthy of and consistent with the commandments of the Gospel, so that whether he comes to them or hears of them during his absence, he may find that they stand firm as members of one body, that is, the body of Christ, and strive together in unity for the spread of the principles of the Gospel among everyone.

entries.section: (5) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Not being afraid of the attacks of the enemy of good, however great the strength of his helpers, for their steadfastness in the faith is a strong proof of their being qualified, by grace, for salvation and for the eternal inheritance; whereas the persecution of the children of God by their opponents is a testimony of their condemnation, which will lead them to eternal destruction.

entries.section: (5) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Steadfastness in the faith and spiritual striving must result in persecution and suffering. And suffering in the Christian view is a gift from God and not a punishment, and it is a sign of love and holy fellowship, behind which is a crown of glory, for suffering is linked to the Kingdom.

entries.section: (5) Spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: You are members with me in the one body; you must strive as I have striven, as you saw in my own person and now hear that I continue in it. For this is the fellowship of sufferings that will lead us to the fellowship of glory with our good Savior.

Accept the sufferings that come upon you for the sake of Christ, who bore all sufferings for you on the Cross, and you will experience His presence with you and rejoice in His consolations, and this will move you to love toil for His sake, not only in worship but in every service.
Unity, humility and striving

entries.section: (1) Unity

paragraphs.text: Comfort: consolation and solace, as it is said in (Col 4:11). St. Paul declares that the aim of all preaching is to proclaim Christ the Savior, and the aim of all service, consolation and support of others is love and not any personal purposes.

And the fellowship among believers has as its aim unity in the Holy Spirit and not any interests, and likewise deep feelings of love and compassion toward others have as their aim unity in the body of Christ. In sum, St. Paul calls all believers to unity in Christ and in love for Him through the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) Unity

paragraphs.text: The Apostle declares that his joy will not be complete unless he is assured that they are of one mind and live in love with one purpose, and that their aim is one for all of them, namely Christ and good works.

entries.section: (1) Unity

paragraphs.text: Vainglory: pride.

If every member of the community had his own thoughts and his own opinion which he tried to impose on others, factions would arise which must end in division. So pride and working for self-glory are rejected in the work of the Gospel, and humility is the healing remedy, so that we give others honor and esteem and regard them as better than ourselves.
Did not the Apostle himself give us an example when he counted himself the last of all and like one born out of due time (1 Cor 15:8)?!

entries.section: (1) Unity

paragraphs.text: A person often concentrates his effort and his concerns on himself, heedless of his brethren, whether in their material or their spiritual affairs. So we must look to the needs of others and work to relieve their pains, to give them rest and to draw them to the spiritual life.

Look to the needs of others, for when you show them love you support them and reveal Christ to them, and you are strengthened as you feel the power of Christ working in you and through you, and you are encouraged as you feel your oneness with others, and the blessings of God overflow upon you.

entries.section: (2) The humility and greatness of Christ

paragraphs.text: The mind to which St. Paul refers is the one he had referred to in the preceding verses, namely the mind of humility and denial of self, and it is the mind of Christ Himself, from whom we must learn.

entries.section: (2) The humility and greatness of Christ

paragraphs.text: "Who, being" is an incorrect Arabic translation; in the original Greek it carries the meaning "who, being and still being," and likewise in English, being in the form of God, and not Was in the form. Accordingly the meaning becomes: He who exists and continues to exist in the divine essential form did not seize or snatch that form for Himself, for He had no need of that, since He is God. That is, He did not try to glorify Himself as God when He became incarnate to redeem us, but He laid aside all His glory and became an ordinary man like us, that is, He took the form of a servant although He is God who fills every place. So He became like us in His humility to save us, but without sin, as we commit it.

entries.section: (2) The humility and greatness of Christ

paragraphs.text: In Christ's being found in human form, He obeyed the will of the Father, and His obedience reached the utmost degree, for He accepted death on the Cross, although He is the Righteous and Holy One, in order to raise us from death to life.

entries.section: (2) The humility and greatness of Christ

paragraphs.text: In return for this humility of His, God raised Him to the surpassing glory, and lifted Him up above the highest heavens and seated Him at His right hand, and this applies to the humanity and not the divinity, because the divinity has its glory continuing without interruption.

Gave Him a name: in the original Greek, "gave Him the name," that is, the word name is definite, meaning that His full glory appeared above every name and person known in heaven or on earth, because He is God.

entries.section: (2) The humility and greatness of Christ

paragraphs.text: Jesus means Jehovah saves, and Jehovah is the majestic name that has the greatest holiness among all names, which makes it obligatory for all creatures, heavenly, earthly and under the earth, to offer worship and bowing to Him. This is an expression to indicate the extent of His authority over all, so that every tongue may praise Him and glorify Him, confessing that Christ is the Lord who has all that the Father has of glory.

In order that you may have glory in heaven, you must humble yourself at the feet of all, as your Christ humbled Himself and then ascended to His glory in the heavens. In addition, when you humble yourself at the feet of people, you will find Christ beside you washing feet, and you will feel His presence with you and rejoice in His companionship.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: Therefore, my beloved, as you have walked in obedience to the Gospel, not only during the time I spent among you but all the more in my absence from you in the body, I ask you to strive constantly as long as you are in the body, while you see God before you and fear Him, so that you reject every sin, and even tremble when you fall, and return with repentance and tears, and He has mercy on you.

And the word "work out" means continuing the striving throughout life, for salvation is not in a moment but throughout the whole of life, so the fear of God remains in our hearts at all times to keep us away from evil. For as long as we are in the world, the enemy of good will not cease trying to make us fall. So let us beware lest we overcome him today and he strike us down tomorrow.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: The Spirit of God creates in us spiritual longings and gives us strength to do good, for every good work is a pleasure to the heavenly Father.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: Murmurings: grumbling.
Disputings: sharp discussion that results in tension.
Every good work that you do, do it quietly and without grumbling, which betrays weak love and little patience, and without sharp discussions that create disagreements among you.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: So that there may be nothing in you deserving reproach and criticism, and that you may be far from all cunning and in a wise Christian simplicity, so that you may be worthy to be children of the heavenly Father, resembling Him in goodness, and live without blemish and have a portion with the ranks of the saints. And because you now live in the midst of a generation that is far from the truth and distorts the truth with cunning, just as the stars guide with their light those who travel in the desert or on the seas, so you shall be like the saints, lights in this age, that those who are far away may be guided by your fragrant conduct.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks the people of Philippi to bear witness to the Gospel in their deeds and words, that they may be a cause of boasting for him in the day in which Christ comes to transfer us to His eternal Kingdom, and the reward of his striving and his service to them will be the crowns of heavenly glory.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: Poured out: the Law of Moses required the pouring out of wine upon the burnt offering presented to God as a sacrifice, and this libation signifies joy. So Paul regards his service and the giving of his life in preaching as if he were being poured out before God to gladden His heart.

The sacrifice of your faith: Paul regards the sufferings that the believers in Philippi undergo for holding fast to their faith as if they were offering their lives as a sacrifice before God, and he rejoices in them.

The Apostle looks at his life as the libation that the priests of the Old Testament used to place on the sacrifices, borrowing this image to express his striving to draw the Gentiles to the faith, regarding their faith in Christ as a living sacrifice. Just as they accept with joy all the tribulations as a declaration of the sacrifice of their faith, so he also rejoices with them all.

entries.section: (3) Striving to complete salvation

paragraphs.text: Because of this service and its results, which are the source of his joy, he asks them to be also glad and rejoicing with him.

Do not be distressed by the multitude of your falls or your weakness or even the coldness of your spiritual feelings, but seek God, who gives you by His Holy Spirit zeal and longings for life with Him and supports you in your striving, in which you persevere to attain the Kingdom. For the grace of God is always with you, and His fear drives sin away from you and makes you grow in the knowledge and love of Him.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: St. Paul puts his trust in the Lord that He will arrange the circumstances for sending Timothy to them soon, so that Paul may be gladdened by knowing their news.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: The Apostle found no one quite like him in love for the people of Philippi and concern for them, because he alone is their spiritual father, at whose hands they believed, and he cares for their shepherding. This is not pride on Paul's part but an expression of the depths of his love. And his sending of Timothy, his son, is as if he himself went to them, because he is his personal representative.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: All: the false teachers and all who oppose Paul, even among those who preach Christ. All of them seek their own interests and desire from their service their personal glory and not the glorifying of the Lord Jesus in their works, seeking what is their own and not what is the Lord Christ's.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: Timothy succeeded in all the trials and tribulations to which he had been exposed before, and remained in his humility, emptying himself. He was like a son to St. Paul in the faith, was brought up and trained at his hands, obeyed this father with all faithfulness, and traveled with him everywhere preaching the Gospel.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: St. Paul decided to send his disciple Timothy as soon as he knew the outcome of the judgment against him, whether the continuation of his imprisonment, or release, or otherwise.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: St. Paul declares his faith and certainty in the love of the Lord, for he is confident that he too will come to them soon when he is released.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: In verses 25 to 30 the Apostle speaks about another disciple, Epaphroditus.

Although the presence of Epaphroditus in Rome was a help to Paul during his imprisonment there, he preferred to send him to his city, Philippi, so that they might rejoice at meeting him, and this is the obligation of the love that seeks not its own but what is for others.

And here St. Paul describes him with several titles that show the extent of Paul's humility, who raises his children to the rank of brotherhood and encourages them and raises them to his own level, making him his partner in service and in preaching the Gospel as a soldier in the army of salvation. Epaphroditus was a delegate from the church of Philippi and carried the love of its people for Paul.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: Epaphroditus longed for the people of Philippi and was grieved at their grief when they learned that he had been sick, for he was dear to them and beloved by them. The tenderness of feelings appears here, for the people of Philippi were moved by his illness and he was moved by their grief for him.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: The illness of Epaphroditus was severe, to the point that he was close to death, but God had mercy on him and healed him.

And Paul feels that God's mercy was directed to him, because he loves Epaphroditus and depends on him for many services. Paul does not do away with feelings of sorrow when loved ones are sick, because Christianity does not abolish human emotions but elevates them.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: Less sorrowful: Paul will grieve at the parting from Epaphroditus, but his grief will be less because he will gladden the people of Philippi by their seeing him.

St. Paul preferred to give up for a time the service of Epaphroditus to him, and to send him to his own people that they might see him and rejoice in him, so that the Apostle also rejoices in their joy.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: The Apostle commands them to receive him and honor him for his labor, for he is not fleeing from his service as some might think.

entries.section: (4) His sending of Timothy and Epaphroditus

paragraphs.text: Epaphroditus risked his life when he visited Paul in prison, exposing himself to dangers. And although they themselves were not able to come to Rome to visit Paul in prison, Epaphroditus performed his service on their behalf and did not refrain from any service Paul entrusted to him.

The illnesses that afflict a person are not the product of chance, but are part of the divine dispensation for our salvation and the proving of our faith. So let us thank the Lord always in every condition, for every condition and in every condition.
Spiritual striving and rejecting false teachings

entries.section: (1) Warning against the teaching of false teachers

paragraphs.text: Finally: in the original Greek, "as for the rest of the discourse."
Safe: it protects you and keeps you secure.

The Apostle calls them to spiritual joy, because the mark of the Christian life is joy in the many graces of God that He has poured out upon us, and moreover joy gives us strength in our spiritual striving. These two matters, that is, the call to joy and the matter that follows it, which is the warning against the false teachers, St. Paul does not tire of repeating, because it keeps them secure from slipping into believing these teachings.

entries.section: (1) Warning against the teaching of false teachers

paragraphs.text: Beware: the Greek word here has the original meaning "always watch out for and avoid." The concision: he means the false teachers, who are converts from a Jewish background and who proclaim the necessity of circumcision for obtaining salvation. Circumcision is called "the concision," that is, the cutting of a part of the body as an outward act without its spiritual meaning.

St. Paul called the false teachers dogs because they tear at the body of the Church, causing division and working against the Gospel, and they proclaim circumcision, which is a cutting in the flesh only, without its spiritual meaning, which is turning away from sin and which was a type of Baptism.

entries.section: (1) Warning against the teaching of false teachers

paragraphs.text: We have no confidence in the flesh: we do not rely on the works of the flesh, that is, the works of the Law, but we live its spiritual meaning in our faith in Christ, in whose salvation we glory.

For we Christians live the true circumcision, that is, the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, which is turning away from evil, and we obey the Lord in the Church and do not rely on bodily circumcision and the other ordinances of the Law as means of justification.

Remain firm in the Church and in her spiritual practices and teachings, and then you will not be exposed to slipping into the strange teachings proclaimed by those who have left the Church, because your habit of the spiritual life with Christ gladdens your heart with it and will make you discover and reject anything foreign to it, lest it separate you from your enjoyment of this joy.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: In the following verses the Apostle Paul mentions seven advantages he had in Judaism that make him surpass the standing of others who glory in the ordinances of the Law. If those Jews think they are something because of their practice of those ordinances, he has advantages that surpass them all.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: Circumcised the eighth day: St. Paul's being circumcised on the eighth day is proof that he was born in the Jewish religion and was not an outsider to it, because proselytes are circumcised on the day they enter the Jewish faith; of the stock of Israel: this confirms the purity of his lineage.

Of the tribe of Benjamin: which had a special standing in Israel, for Benjamin is the only son of Jacob who was born in the Promised Land, and his tribe also remained attached to the tribe of Judah after the division, that is, holding fast to worship in the temple at Jerusalem.
A Hebrew: born of Hebrew parents, and he kept the Hebrew tongue although he was born in a Gentile land.

Hebrews: that is, the descendants of Abraham, because Eber was one of the forefathers of Abraham (Gen 11:16), and Abraham is called the Hebrew because he crossed the river and left his kindred and his family, as God told him, to live in the land of Canaan and worship Him there (Acts 7:2). A Pharisee: he learned and was trained in the stricter Pharisaic school, so his duty was to keep the details of the Law.

Paul declares that he is truly a Jew like all other Jews, so he affirms his circumcision and clarifies his lineage, and even his superiority, since he was among those strict in holding to the Law, that is, a Pharisee.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: Before Paul's faith in Christ, his chief occupation was the destruction of the Church and the persecution of Christians, and he was very strict in carrying out the commandments of the Law, so that he did not violate its teachings in anything throughout his former life, and no one can blame him for any shortcoming on his part.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: All the previous advantages, which many of the Jews regard as great gains, Paul considered to be of no benefit and as nothing if they hindered him from knowing Christ.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: What St. Paul lost by leaving the Jewish religion when he believed in Christ, he considered as nothing compared with what he gained, namely his new life in the Christian faith.

entries.section: (2) Glorying in Christ and not in the Law

paragraphs.text: My union with Christ in the Church gives me security, and I obtain salvation by my sonship to her, whereas outside the Church is loss and eternal perdition, because the Law was unable to grant man righteousness; man cannot be justified by himself, but by faith in Christ he arrives at the state of righteousness and holiness.

All that the world may give us does not satisfy our souls, but the knowledge of Christ gives rest to our hearts and grants us a peace that surpasses all understanding. Therefore may we give priority in our time to God before the preoccupations of the world and its comfort and its pleasures, for they are all passing and do not satisfy our souls.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: St. Paul's rejection of all the previous advantages was for the sake of knowing Christ truly, and of grasping the victory He achieved over all the powers of evil when He raised Himself by His divine power after the death of the Cross, and drew him up from the death of sin to the life of fellowship with Him, accepting every suffering the world imposes on him, to share with the Lord Jesus His sufferings for the sake of righteousness, and he longs for martyrdom, being conformed to His death.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Apostle hopes to rise on the great day of judgment in the resurrection of the righteous to eternal life. And he highlights here the difficulty of attaining this and that it requires striving and vigilance.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Apostle wanted to teach us that as long as we are in the body we must strive toward perfection until the last breath. He expresses here clearly a life of pursuit and striving until we reach salvation and eternal life, that blessed end for which the Lord Christ sought him and turned him from a persecutor of the Church into a great apostle defending the Christian faith.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: After St. Paul considers what he has done during his life, he sees that he has not yet reached the required level. Much growth is still needed, so the only thing he sets as the foundation of his present striving is to refuse to look at the past of his life with its errors, and to concentrate his thoughts and his effort on his responsibility toward his righteousness and his Church.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: Prize: reward.
The goal for which he strives is God's holy calling for the salvation of all, and his being crowned with the crown of glory that the just Judge will grant him on that day.

To the degree that you feel the greatness of being with God and the glory of the Kingdom, you hold fast to striving in the spiritual life and reject every sin by repentance, and you even cut off all sources of evil and persevere in your striving by the help of God, who supports you and encourages you until you reach your goal.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: This: that is, the constant pursuit in spiritual striving.
Perfect: those who are pursuing perfection.

Let us who are spiritually mature have this mind, which is the mind of Christ. But if some of you are occupied with another mind contrary to this and are exposed to deviations on the way, God will reveal the truth to you by His Spirit who dwells in you.

entries.section: (3) Constant pursuit of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: Whereto we have already attained: our previous spiritual practice of prayers, fasts and various acts of worship. Rule: the spiritual order by which we worship God and serve Him.
Mind the same thing: the importance of continuing in spiritual striving.
What we practiced of spiritual striving in our past spiritual life, let us persevere in it, assured of the importance of the constant pursuit toward the Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) The end of the wicked and the righteous

paragraphs.text: Because the Apostle imitates Christ in his life, he asks the Philippians to imitate him also in his life and conduct, and also to imitate their spiritual guides, who are an example to them.

entries.section: (4) The end of the wicked and the righteous

paragraphs.text: Walk: they behave in evil and strange heresies.
The enemies of the cross of Christ, by their deviant thoughts, lead people astray from the Savior Christ who was crucified for our redemption.

As for these who followed the strange teachings and whom the Apostle warned against being influenced by their opinions, he repeats here the warning against them despite his love for them and his weeping over them. The Apostle hates their evils and their sin and not their persons, for he regards them as erring sons.

entries.section: (4) The end of the wicked and the righteous

paragraphs.text: The destiny of these false teachers is eternal destruction, for they are always hastening to satisfy their whims and worldly desires, and they do evil and boast of doing it.

entries.section: (4) The end of the wicked and the righteous

paragraphs.text: But as for us, because our original homeland is heaven, we walk spiritually like the heavenly ones, eagerly expecting the coming of Christ at His Second Coming, and awaiting His promise to save us from the misery of the present world and to let us enjoy His eternal glory.

entries.section: (4) The end of the wicked and the righteous

paragraphs.text: For it is He who will change this weak body of ours, which is subject to sickness, pain and disfigurement and liable to sin and falling, into a glorified body without sin, like His body with which He rose from the dead, for He who was able to conquer death by Himself has the power to give life to our mortal bodies.

May we look every day to our goal, which is heaven, so that we walk in a manner worthy of life there, in purity and love for everyone, and always contemplate the life of the angels and the saints in heaven, and seek their intercession and imitate their conduct, so that we taste the earnest of the Kingdom while we are on earth and our longing for it increases. Virtues, steadfastness and giving

entries.section: (1) Steadfastness and mutual understanding

paragraphs.text: Therefore, you whom I love and long for, you who are the cause of my joy and the reason for my obtaining the crown with which the Lord will crown me in eternal glory, I ask you to hold fast to the faith of Christ and His commandments.

entries.section: (1) Steadfastness and mutual understanding

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks two women servants in Philippi, "Euodias and Syntyche," to end the disagreements between them so that they may agree on one mind, which is the mind of Christ.

entries.section: (1) Steadfastness and mutual understanding

paragraphs.text: True yokefellow: it is thought that he is Luke, who accompanied him (Acts 16:10-17), or Epaphroditus, the writer of this letter (v. 23), or one of Paul's disciples who assisted him in the service of the church of Philippi.

Give up your opinion even if it is right, in order to preserve the peace of the ministry, because being upset will cause many to stumble and make you troubled. And take care to reconcile those who differ with one another in order to remove all tension; in this you will be a son of God and a peacemaker.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: The Apostle calls for constant joy and repeats his call to rejoice to stress that it is necessary, for nothing in the world can take away the feelings of joy from believers, whatever the circumstances or troubles or tribulations around them, because the source of joy is God who dwells in the heart; but care must be taken that the joy be in Christ and pleasing to Him and not in the manner of the world.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: The Apostle commands them to adorn themselves with patience and keep away from anger, which means a call to a life of surrender and endurance, and to show this virtue to people not by way of pretense or boasting but so that people may see the virtues in Christianity. Our life on earth is short, and we always expect the Lord's coming to be near, therefore we readily give up many of our material rights and bear patiently with those who wrong us, since our eyes are fixed on the Kingdom and the Second Coming of Christ.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: He also asks them to cast off from themselves the cares of life and all anxiety, and not to be troubled and confused before trials, but to hold fast to prayer, for it is the only way to true rest and a sure remedy for anxiety, and let them lift up their personal needs in supplication, always accompanied by thanksgiving.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: The Apostle wishes them the peace of God, who is able to keep their hearts and direct all their thought toward Christ who strengthens them, because however much human wisdom a person attains, he cannot attain such divine peace, which surpasses the level of the human mind.

You can enjoy peace and joy, the desire of all people, if your relationship with God is strong, and specifically if you are devoted to prayer, not only at its appointed times in your inner room and in the church, but throughout the day. And if you meet with wrongs from others and the problems of life, place them before God in prayer, confident of His care and His providence, and continue to delight in speaking with Him.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: Honest: great and dignified.
Pure: clean from evil.

In sum, he asks them to practice this daily conduct in their Christian life, holding fast to the truth, that is, being truthful in what belongs to others as in what belongs to themselves. And let their thoughts be occupied with all that is true in the sight of God and all that is noble and of great worth. And let them follow justice in all their relationships with God and people: with God by keeping His rights, and with people by wronging no one. And let them preserve purity of thought and seek it with all their hearts and do what pleases God and people. And let them have a good reputation and good conduct before everyone, and seek to acquire virtues and perform every deed that deserves praise.

entries.section: (2) A call to virtues and Christian conduct

paragraphs.text: He also hopes that they will walk in all that they learned and heard from him about the life of holiness and saw him doing as well. And the God of peace, whom He grants to them, will be with them and help them in their spiritual striving to acquire these virtues.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: The Apostle expresses his joy and thanks to the Lord and to them, likening their work for him to a tree blossoming a second time and putting forth new leaves. For the church of Philippi had not been able to send him material help for a long time because of the difficulty of travel on the roads, and then the Lord allowed them to care for him again after they had waited a long time for an opportunity to do so.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: What he told them about his joy is not for the material help in itself so much as for their love that appeared in their gifts. For since he became a Christian he learned how to live a life of contentment, satisfaction and sufficiency with what he has.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: He knows how to live on little and be satisfied with it, and even to keep some of it in reserve. In all the circumstances he faced he is always content in the Lord, whether in hunger or fullness, in abundance of material goods or in their lack, and the secret of this is Christ who dwells in him.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: For from Christ he draws the strength and ability to face all circumstances and overcome all difficulties.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: St. Paul appreciates the labor of love of the people of Philippi and thanks them for all that they did and gave as gifts for his sake, since he felt their sharing with him in his affliction during the period of his imprisonment.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: After St. Paul preached to the people of Philippi and left their province, Macedonia, no church shared with him in giving gifts as they did. And here he magnifies their giving, so he regards them as partners in his ministry.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: St. Paul does not forget their sending more than once to help him provide for the needs of the ministry, and that was when he was in Thessalonica.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: All the sincere love they offer is added to their account in the Kingdom. Paul does not want them to think that he is concerned with seeking the gift, but he asks God to reward them with abundant fruit here and in eternity.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: Their offerings have supplied all his needs and even overflowed beyond the need, and he received from Epaphroditus their gifts, which are with the Lord sacrifices of love, acceptable and of a sweet savor, as was said of the sacrifices of the Old Testament, which were for acceptance and pleasure (Lev 1:9, 13).

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: Therefore he asks the Lord to supply all their needs according to His unlimited riches and by the merits of Jesus Christ, in whom their offerings become pleasing and acceptable to the Father, so that He rewards them in this age and in the age to come.

entries.section: (3) His thanks to them for their gifts and their reward

paragraphs.text: At the close of the letter he gives glory to God our Father forever.

How great is Paul's appreciation of the gifts of the people of Philippi. May you show your appreciation for what others do toward you, and likewise for everything good in them, for words of encouragement are needed by all people, old and young, especially if you are going to have to blame someone, you must begin your words to him with encouragement and praise.

entries.section: (4) Closing greetings

paragraphs.text: The Apostle concludes his letter by presenting his greetings to every believer in the church of Philippi, and he sends to the people of Philippi the greetings of his fellow workers in the ministry and his assistants in the preaching in Rome.

entries.section: (4) Closing greetings

paragraphs.text: He also sends the greetings of all the members of the Church in Rome and of the members of the imperial guard in Caesar's household, whom the Apostle led to the knowledge of Christ.

entries.section: (4) Closing greetings

paragraphs.text: The Apostle began his letter with grace and ends it also by asking grace for them, grace which is the work of God with the human soul.
The last sentence in the letter was written to clarify the place where the letter was written and the person by whom it was sent.

How beautiful is the fellowship among the members of the Church in the exchange of greetings, love and good wishes. May we care for fellowship and affection within our family and with our relatives and in the Church, for this gives rest and satisfaction to the soul, as well as good relationships with others.
